Lenovo takes on the MacBook Neo with its colorful new IdeaPad Vibe laptop.

Unveiled at Lenovo Innovation World ahead of IFA, the Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe is clearly taking aim at Apple's most affordable and popular MacBook Neo, and on paper, it looks like a worthy match. The laptop can be configured with either a 14-inch or 15-inch OLED display, has a thickness of 14.9mm, and a starting weight of 2.87 pounds. It's thicker and larger than Apple's laptop, but the weight difference isn't too significant. Lenovo says the Vibe will be available in both plastic and metal versions.

But it does look pretty eye-catching: Lenovo has partnered with Pantone to offer the IdeaPad Vibe in 7 different colors, including:

Dreamy Violet: A subtle violet hue with depth that evokes calm, bringing a sense of peace and comfort. Spicy Gold: A rich golden tone blending warmth and energy, radiating confidence and approachability. Zen Green: A nature-inspired green that evokes balance and harmony, encouraging you to slow down. Chill Blue: An icy blue with a crisp, modern feel that energizes and refreshes. Radiant Coral: A warm, uplifting hue with an optimistic orange flair, radiating friendliness and positive energy. Moody Blue: A deep blue tone that conveys reliability and confidence, exuding elegance. Lowkey Grey: A timeless grey that conveys strength, stability, and understated taste.

The keyboard also features swappable keycaps, allowing you to customize and create different color combinations.

But good looks are only part of the story, as Lenovo has packed this laptop with some pretty attractive specs: two USB-A ports, one HDMI port, two USB-C ports, a headphone jack, and even a microSD card reader. There's also a 5MP webcam (with a physical privacy shutter), an optional backlit keyboard, and an optional touchscreen on the 15-inch model.

But what about the internal specs?

Users can choose between an AMD Ryzen AI 400 chip or a Qualcomm Snapdragon X chip. The AMD model supports up to 32GB of RAM and is user-upgradeable. Configurations also include up to 1TB of storage, which is also upgradeable and comes with dual slots. The Snapdragon version supports up to 24GB of RAM, with storage still upgradeable but RAM is not. Lenovo says an Intel version will come later.

The Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe will launch in two waves. The AMD model goes on sale in October, followed by the Snapdragon model in November. Both start at $699.99, matching Apple's MacBook Neo after its RAM upgrade price increase.

Lenovo also launched the IdeaCentre AIO I alongside it, an all-in-one desktop with a 24-inch or 27-inch display, similar color options to the Vibe, starting at $939, also available from November.
